rejected.title: Feudalism
card: Feudalism was the system that organised land and power in much of medieval Europe. Land was the main source of wealth, so whoever held it held power.
The king granted large areas of land to powerful lords. In return, the lords promised loyalty and had to supply soldiers when the king needed them.
Lords then gave parts of their land to knights, who promised to fight for them. Each person owed duties to the one who gave them land.
At the bottom were the peasants. They worked the land and did not hold power in the system.
rejected.remember: Land went from king to lords to knights in return for loyalty and service, and peasants farmed it.

a.q: Why did a medieval king grant land to his lords?
opts: To gain their loyalty and soldiers
To collect rent from them in coins
To let peasants own their own farms
To pay for the building of churches
a.why: The king held land, which was wealth, and he traded it for loyalty and soldiers. The option about rent is wrong because the lords gave loyalty and soldiers in return, not coins.
a.clue: Think about what the lords promised in return.

b.q: Sir Edmund holds land from Lord Aldric and promises to fight for him. Who is the land granted to Edmund most likely to be worked by?
opts: Peasants who farm the land for him
The king's own royal soldiers
Other lords who also hold land
Knights who serve Lord Aldric
b.why: Land passed from the king to lords to knights, and the peasants below them worked it. Other knights are wrong because knights received land in return for fighting, not for farming it.
b.clue: Which group did the farm work rather than the fighting?

version.remember: Land went from king to lords to knights in return for loyalty and service, and peasants farmed it.

a.q: What did a medieval lord give the king in return for a grant of land?
opts: Loyalty and soldiers when needed
Rent paid each year in coins
A share of every peasant's harvest
Money to build the king's churches
a.why: Under feudalism the king traded land for the lords' loyalty and for soldiers when he needed them. Rent in coins is tempting, but the grant was paid for with loyalty and military service, not money.
a.clue: The king needed an army as well as people he could trust.

b.q: Sir Edmund is a knight who holds land granted to him by Lord Aldric. Under feudalism, who does Edmund owe service to, and what kind?
opts: Lord Aldric, by fighting for him
Lord Aldric, by paying him in coins
The peasants, by farming their land
The king, by farming the royal land
b.why: Each person owed duties to the one who gave them land, and knights promised to fight for their lord. Paying Lord Aldric in coins names the right person but the wrong kind of service.
b.clue: Who gave Edmund his land, and what did knights promise?

b.best: Lord Aldric, by fighting for him
